title: scaffold-specification.json contract (post-materialize)
description: Structural contract for asic/<module>/Verification/simulation-plan/scaffold-specification.json, validated at the sim-plan Completion Gate AFTER the materialize-scaffold verb has run. Strongly validates LLM-authored fields; tolerates (does not deep-validate) the interface/transaction objects materialize-scaffold injects into agents[] (their content is owned by materialize-scaffold + sim/_guards._agent_io). Referential integrity (observer/inports/seqs/sequence_ref resolving to declared agents/sequences) is NOT expressible here; the check-scaffold gate's semantic layer enforces it.

feature.description: The features.json id this test exercises. Required: it is the key materialize-scaffold resolves feature_name through, and the only thing that makes a result traceable.

test_id.description: Stable per-test identifier; the regression log keys results by it.

suites.description: Which suites run this test. YOUR judgment as the plan author, not a script's: `make smoke` runs the smoke set, `make regress` runs everything. A smoke test is one whose failure means the design is broken badly enough that running the rest is pointless — pick them by that, not by position in the list.

feature_name.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the matching features.json entry's `name`, verbatim. It is what the Feature column of case-results-summary.md prints, so a human reads this rather than a bare id.

inports.description: The agents[].name values whose monitor streams feed the RM — one analysis_imp port each. Name the AGENT, not its transaction type: render-scaffold builds the type as <module>_<agent>_txn where it needs one, so a name written here in txn form would have to be un-wrapped and re-wrapped to reach the same string.

observer.description: The ONE agents[].name whose monitor stream the scoreboard compares against the RM. Omitted only when a single agent is declared; with more than one, omitting it is ambiguous and the gate rejects it.

intent.description: What this testpoint drives and why — the stimulus/intent the env and conformance-fix children read as the intent source. Distinct from the checks: `inlined_check_hints` says how each covered check is verified, this says what situation is being created.

covers.description: The `check-hints/<child>.json` check_ids this testpoint verifies. Present with an explicit empty array on a scenario testpoint you invented — omitted and `[]` are not the same claim, and an empty one traces to no feature.

inlined_check_hints.description: Script-injected by `simplan materialize-scaffold` (never hand-authored): the precise check semantics from the authored `check-hints/<child>.json`, materialized into this testpoint via its `covers[]`. `implementation_detail` is verbatim-if-present-else-summary; `source_feature` is what `feature_count` traces through.

power_scenarios.description: One entry per scenario materialized from references/power-scenarios-template.md's standard set. This is the only home — verification-plan.md §4 points here and restates no field. Two of these are load-bearing across the stage boundary: power-analysis's own result.schema.json REQUIRES corner_intent and duration_cycles, so an omitted one would surface as a downstream envelope failure rather than here.

scenario.description: The standard set's scenario name, materialized for this module (e.g. "200MB/s (low-power off)").

data_state.description: Traffic level this scenario drives: none / no traffic / business_flow / full-toggle, per the standard set.

corner_intent.description: PVT corner this scenario is annotated at (e.g. "SS/125C"). Equivalent scenarios reusing one sequence_ref keep distinct corner_intent — that is what the SAIF-per-ID dedup preserves.

sequence_ref.description: A sequences[].name. The only field emit_power_tests reads; it groups by this and runs each group once.
